official.deadline_note: There is no single EU-wide deadline. Each EMJM consortium publishes its own application deadline on the programme website; the EACEA states most programmes require applications between October and January for courses starting the following academic year.
official.application_cycle: Applications typically submitted between October and January for courses commencing the following academic year; the catalogue is updated annually
official.status_note: The EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue lists the master's programmes currently supported by the EU and is updated annually; students apply directly to the consortium of their chosen programme. Austria is among the partner countries listed in the catalogue filter.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Erasmus+ Programme Guide, Erasmus Mundus action: selected projects cannot charge student application fees, and projects cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to student participation in the course to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders.
official.funding_period: per month for the full programme duration (up to 24 months)
benefits: Full scholarship for the best-ranked students worldwide
Scholarship covers travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs
No tuition fees or other mandatory participation costs charged to scholarship holders
Contribution to individual needs of students with disabilities, unit costs from EUR 3 000 to EUR 60 000
Joint or multiple diploma awarded on completion, with a joint diploma supplement
eligibility: Hold a first higher education degree (bachelor's), or be in the last year of bachelor studies
Graduate before the master's programme starts
Bachelor's equivalent level of learning is acceptable if officially recognised under the degree-awarding country's legislation
Open to students from all over the world
Students who previously obtained an EMJM scholarship are not eligible for an additional scholarship
Scholarship is awarded only to full-time students
requirements: Full-time enrolment for the entire programme duration (scholarship awarded in full only)
Compulsory physical mobility: at least two study periods in two countries different from the country of residence, each of at least one semester
Sign a Student Agreement with the consortium upon enrolment
selection_criteria: Scholarships are awarded to the best-ranked students applying worldwide
Student selection is the sole responsibility of the EMJM consortium and must be organised transparently, impartially and equitably
Geographical balance rule: no more than 10% of scholarships awarded during project implementation should go to candidates of the same nationality
coverage: Tuition fees and other mandatory participation costs waived for scholarship holders
application_method: Apply directly to the consortium running the chosen Erasmus Mundus Joint Master
Consult the chosen programme's official website for study details, participating universities, entry requirements and application steps (with and without scholarship)
Contact the consortium directly for information on courses, application procedures and scholarship availability
official.application_route: Apply online directly to the consortium of the specific EMJM programme; there is no central European Commission application for students.
official.study_mode: Full-time (the scholarship can only be awarded in full and to full-time students)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to students from all over the world; no nationality or residency restriction, but a geographical balance rule limits scholarships to a maximum of 10% per nationality
official.international_eligibility: Yes - students worldwide may apply, and EMJM scholarships can be offered to students from all countries
official.duration: 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits)
official.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are prestigious international master's programmes, jointly designed and delivered by a consortium of higher education institutions from at least three different countries, involving study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence. Full scholarships are available for the best-ranked students worldwide, covering participation costs and contributing to travel, visa and living costs.
official.region: Europe and partner countries worldwide (delivered in at least two countries; Austria-based programmes are listed in the EACEA catalogue)
official.program_type: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) - joint or multiple degree

verification.notes: Amount (EUR 1 400/month, max 24 months), coverage (travel, visa, installation, subsistence) and the fee-waiver rule were confirmed on the Erasmus+ Programme Guide Erasmus Mundus action page (current version, part of the 2026 Call); eligibility, duration and the October-January application window were confirmed on the Erasmus+ student page and the EACEA catalogue page. Required documents, English tests and exact deadlines are set by each consortium and are not published centrally.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a scholarship scheme, not one master: you pick an Austria-linked Erasmus Mundus consortium from the EACEA catalogue and compete for its scholarship, so your real task is choosing the right consortium and hitting its own deadline rather than one EU deadline. The award is a fixed EUR 1 400 per month for the whole 12, 18 or 24 months of the programme (up to EUR 33 600), with travel, visa and installation costs included and tuition waived for scholarship holders. Most consortia open applications between October and January for a September/October start the following year, and applications go straight to the consortium's own portal. Because only the top-ranked applicants per consortium are funded, most experienced applicants submit to three to five programmes.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year bachelor students and recent graduates with strong transcripts who want a two-country mobility master and can document an officially recognised first degree before the programme starts.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist 3-5 Erasmus Mundus programmes that include an Austrian partner from the EACEA catalogue, and confirm on each consortium website that it currently awards scholarships for your intake (some listed programmes do not)
Write down each chosen consortium's own deadline and document list; do not rely on an October-January window, as several programmes close earlier or run rolling selection
Secure a transcript and degree certificate plus official translation showing you will hold a recognised first degree before the course begins
Verify you can attend in person: compulsory mobility across two countries, each period of at least one semester, cannot be replaced by online study
If you already held an EMJM scholarship, confirm eligibility first - former recipients cannot be awarded a second one
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a single consortium, where scholarship places number in the tens per intake and only the best-ranked applicants are funded
Missing the consortium's own deadline because the EU publishes no central closing date
Assuming every programme in the catalogue funds scholarships - some are near the end of their funding period or hold temporary use of the name
A weak or generic motivation letter that does not address the specific consortium's mobility structure and mobility track choice
Submitting a degree that is not recognised in the awarding country without supporting equivalence documentation
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award is a fixed monthly unit cost, so personal spending beyond subsistence, health or liability items not included in it, and any pre-arrival costs incurred before the scholarship period are self-funded; consortia are forbidden to charge application fees or tuition to scholarship holders, so those cannot be passed on to you.
document_audit: There is no EU-wide document list: each consortium posts its own required set on its programme website, so treat the programme page as the only authority
Expect proof of a first degree or a recognised equivalence, often with certified translations into the language the consortium specifies
Language proof requirements are set per consortium and are not published by the Commission, so check the specific programme's language policy before applying
alerts: Deadlines differ per consortium - the October-January pattern is a guide from the Commission, not a closing date
A 10% nationality cap applies to scholarship allocation, so your odds depend on how many of your countrymen apply to the same consortium
Former EMJM scholarship holders are explicitly excluded from a second scholarship
The catalogue is refreshed yearly, so last year's programme list may name courses that no longer receive EU scholarships
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You submit the academic file online to the consortium (usually with a motivation letter, transcripts, degree proof and language evidence), the consortium ranks applicants and offers scholarships to its top-ranked candidates, and successful students then sign a Student Agreement and a study agreement fixing their mobility track before enrolment.
